title: Llama.cpp on a jailbroken PS5: run any GGUF model natively on the console
content:
Your PS5 runs the language model. Every device on your network uses it.
llama.cpp on the console's GPU, with OpenAI and Anthropic APIs and a screen made for the TV.
Get the app · Website · Get started · Issues
New: decision models, powered by Ollaya. PS5LM now runs Jev-like
decision models (d1, Clef, OpenJev and more) on the GPU and answers the same /v1/systemone
API as Ollaya: typed decisions with calibrated probabilities, in a fraction of a second.
PS5LM is for anyone with a jailbroken PS5 who wants a private model server at home. It loads a GGUF model onto the console's GPU and serves it to your laptop, your phone and your coding tools. It needs no PC while it runs, no cloud and no account.
  
Qwen 3.5 9B answering requests from a laptop on a PS5 Slim. Click for the video.
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
Home, Models, Console, API and Settings on the TV.
- It runs on the GPU. llama.cpp's Vulkan backend on the console's RDNA 2 GPU, with 11.4 GB of the shared memory for the model and its context. Every architecture and quantization llama.cpp knows comes along.
- It answers your network. OpenAI's /v1/chat/completions, Anthropic's /v1/messages (Claude Code
works against it) and a chat page in any browser. Point a client at http://<console>:8081 and use
any model name: the loaded one answers.
- It decides, too. Load a decision model and the console answers TypeSafe's /v1/systemone:
choice, score and yes-or-no questions about text and images, the API Ollaya serves on a PC.
- It shows its work. Every request streams across the TV as a chat: which device asked, what it asked, and the reply as it is written. Square sends a demo and Triangle opens a keyboard, so the console can be tried from the couch.
- It watches the console. A Console page charts temperature, power, GPU and CPU load over the last two minutes or the last hour, beside a table of every reading.
- It picks what fits. The planner reads each GGUF and gives it the longest context and best cache that fit the memory free. A Suggested list holds models measured on the console, and the app downloads from Hugging Face by itself, to internal storage, the M.2 drive or a USB drive.
- It reads images. Models with an image projector (Gemma 4, MiniCPM-V, d1) take pictures in chat and in decisions.
Ollaya runs open decision models on a PC the way Ollama runs language models. PS5LM brings the same idea to the console: a decision model reads a state and answers typed questions in one forward pass, with no text generated.
curl http://<console>:8081/v1/systemone -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": "I was charged twice this month. Refund me or I cancel.",
  "questions": {
    "intent": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What does the customer want?",
               "criteria": {"refund": null, "information": null, "cancel": null}},
    "angry":  {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is the customer angry?"}
  }
}'
The Suggested list has d1 Omni 600M, d1 3B and Clef Flash. Any GGUF that carries llama.cpp's decision metadata loads the same way, and the app labels it a decision model.
You need a PS5 on firmware 7.00 to 13.60, jailbroken, with these payloads loaded:
- Download ps5lm-app-vX.Y.Z.zip from the latest release and unzip it.
- Copy the PPSA99575 folder to /data/homebrew over FTP. ShadowMountPlus adds PS5LM to the
home screen.
- Open PS5LM, go to Models > Suggested and get a model. Or copy a .gguf to /data/PS5LM/models, or to PS5LM/models on a USB drive.
- Load it. Once Home says Ready, open http://<console>:8081 in a browser, or point your OpenAI or
Anthropic client at it.
To update, copy the new folder over the old one. Settings, models and downloads stay in
/data/PS5LM. Using it from coding tools (opencode, Codex, Claude Code) is in
docs/CLI.md.
C++ on ps5-homebrew-ui, llama.cpp with ggml-vulkan on PS5_Vulkan's RADV, built on Linux.

report.summary: PS5LM brings llama.cpp's Vulkan backend to jailbroken PS5s, turning the console into a local GPU-accelerated GGUF model server with OpenAI and Anthropic APIs.
report.background: Local LLM inference has moved from data centers to laptops, phones and single-board computers, driven by llama.cpp, Ollama and GGUF quantization. The PlayStation 5 is an unlikely but potent target: its AMD RDNA 2 GPU and 16 GB of shared memory are roughly comparable to a mid-range discrete GPU, and the homebrew scene has already ported Vulkan via PS5_Vulkan and RADV driver patches. PS5LM builds on abhi245y's native PS5LM Plus app, BlackBearReloaded's ps5-homebrew-ui, and John Törnblom's SDK, wrapping llama.cpp into a TV-friendly server. It also rides a newer trend: 'decision models' like Ollaya's d1 and Clef that answer typed questions with calibrated probabilities in a single forward pass rather than generating text. The result is a no-PC, no-cloud, no-account inference box that sits under your television.
key_points: GPU-native inference: PS5LM runs llama.cpp's ggml-Vulkan backend directly on the console's RDNA 2 GPU, allocating 11.4 GB of shared memory to the model and its context. Every architecture and quantization llama.cpp supports works, so users are not locked to a curated model list — any compatible GGUF can be dropped onto the M.2 drive, USB stick or internal storage.

It is a real network server, not a demo. The console exposes OpenAI's /v1/chat/completions and Anthropic's /v1/messages at port 8081, so tools like Claude Code, Codex and opencode connect without modification. Any model name in a request is answered by whichever model is currently loaded, and a browser chat page works on any device on the LAN.

A second API serves decision models. Loading a GGUF with llama.cpp decision metadata unlocks /v1/systemone, which answers choice, score and yes/no questions about text and images — the same API Ollaya serves on a PC. Bundled options include d1 Omni 600M, d1 3B and Clef Flash, returning typed answers in a fraction of a second.

The living-room layer is unusually polished. A Home/Models/Console/API/Settings UI renders on the TV, every request streams in as a chat showing which device asked and what it asked, and a Console page charts temperature, power and GPU/CPU load. Square triggers a demo and Triangle opens an on-screen keyboard, so it can be driven entirely from the couch.

Setup assumes a jailbroken console on firmware 7.00 to 13.60. Users unzip a release, FTP the PPSA99575 folder into /data/homebrew, and let ShadowMountPlus surface it on the home screen. A planner picks the longest context each GGUF can fit, and the app downloads suggested models from Hugging Face by itself.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is a small but pointed demonstration that capable inference no longer needs cloud GPUs or expensive hardware: a games console bought for other reasons becomes a private model host. For developers, it delivers OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints on a machine that draws gaming-console power and costs nothing extra to run, which lowers the barrier to testing agentic tools like Claude Code against local weights. For regular users, the draw is privacy and zero marginal cost — prompts never leave the house. The caveats are real, though: it requires a jailbroken PS5 on specific firmware, sits in a legal gray zone with Sony, caps out around 11.4 GB of usable memory for weights and context, and will trail a dedicated GPU in throughput.
report.tools: Follow llama.cpp and ggml for the inference core and quantization formats, and Ollama or LM Studio for comparison desktop setups. On the PS5 side, watch PS5_Vulkan, ps5-homebrew-ui, the ps5 SDK, ShadowMountPlus and ps5-exporter. For model discovery, browse Hugging Face GGUF repositories, including the decision models d1 Omni 600M, d1 3B and Clef Flash from Ollaya/TypeSafe. Client-side, Claude Code, Codex and opencode all speak the APIs PS5LM exposes, making them the fastest way to try it.
